thesis: The manuscript defends a conditional constraint on implementation: when legitimate authorization reserves a practical public power to discontinue specified governance, implementers must proportionately preserve the means of exercising that power. The introduction states that implementers 'owe proportionate preparation for its exercise.' Mere temporariness or promised reconsideration does not establish this reservation. Independent duties to dependent people constrain both preparation and eventual discontinuation. If the reservation cannot reasonably be maintained, implementers must obtain changed authorization, reduce the experiment, or refrain from exceeding permission. Section 8 adds a conditional reason to restore a reserved power lost through preventable implementation choices; necessary continuation does not retrospectively authorize those choices.
claimed_contribution: Section 7 describes a 'focused authorization argument' rather than discovery of an ethical duty to prepare for exit. Its distinguishing elements are the separation of reporting, reconsideration, and practical reservation; the allocation of authority to decide whether an exit option may be sacrificed; the distinction between protecting assistance and preserving its disputed governing arrangement; and reasons for repair that do not require citizens to have expected compliance. The strongest reading is a specification of limited public permission, with operational and remedial implications, rather than a general principle against irreversible policy.

findings.manuscript_location: §3, 'Why a power requires material support': 'respecting a material limit can require positive action'; §6, 'Institutions, rights, and emergencies': 'Responsibilities nevertheless follow actual powers'; §7, 'The contribution and its predecessors': 'a focused authorization argument'.
findings.claim: The literature positioning omits close precedents for making conditional permission operational through preparation, protected obligations, and renewed approval.
findings.analysis: This is demonstrated additional overlap, not a demonstrated refutation or a claim of wholesale anticipation. NEA's 2001 report, §5.6 and §§6.1–6.4, connects claimed retrievability with feasible methods, monitoring, expertise, funding, and regulatory arrangements. BVI's 2020 guidelines require a wind-down plan protecting customer obligations, prior approval for changes, and implementation of contingency arrangements after refusal to license. Philipsen and colleagues also connect limited public powers with explicit exit strategies. These sources bring authorization and practical preparation together more closely than a contrast with welfare-valued flexibility alone suggests. None of the inspected passages establishes the manuscript's complete moral argument for repairing a lost collective power. See [NEA](https://www.oecd-nea.org/upload/docs/application/pdf/2020-12/nea3140.pdf), [BVI guidelines](https://www.bvifsc.vg/sites/default/files/documents/AML_CFT/Virtual_Assets/the_regulatory_sandbox_guidelines_.pdf), and [Philipsen et al.](https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/rego.12375).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The implementation package cannot carry a broad originality claim. The surviving contribution must remain the explicit normative explanation of a particular public reservation and its remedial implications. The manuscript already limits its ambition substantially, so this finding does not defeat its conditional conclusion.
findings.repair_conditions: Compare these precedents directly and identify what the paired-mandate argument and breach-based repair reason add beyond existing permission conditions and exit-planning requirements.

surviving_contribution: A defensible remainder is the integration of three distinctions: a reserved public power versus an opportunity to reconsider; an obligation to maintain assistance versus an obligation to retain its governing arrangement; and present necessity versus retrospective justification. Section 3's 'difference is who may settle the tradeoff and under what mandate' identifies the central normative claim. Section 8's statement that repair has a reason because 'the institution removed a public power that belonged within its mandate' extends it beyond ordinary prospective planning. Existing sources substantially anticipate exit preparation, conditional permissions, safeguards, and expectation-independent transition protection. I did not locate the complete combination, especially the specific repair argument, in the passages actually inspected. That supports a limited claim of specification and synthesis, not established priority or an independently new moral principle.
remaining_questions: §7 explicitly allows that the proposal may specify 'familiar duties of limited delegation, autonomy, or justice.' What argumentative work remains after applying ordinary duties to respect a valid condition and remedy its breach? This is an unresolved question about theoretical contribution, not a demonstrated inconsistency.

§3 says administrators cannot 'replace the adopted allocation of authority with its preferred package.' Eule's 1987 abstract presents an earlier temporal-delegation account of limits on binding successors. Its complete argument was inaccessible, so the proximity of that account to this particular inference remains unverified.

§8 grounds repair in removal of a reserved power, 'even where nobody previously expected compliance.' The inspected precedents do not settle whether this is a distinctive remedial ground or an application of general institutional duties following unauthorized action.

§2 permits a reservation to arise from an 'authoritative explanation of a mandate.' How far can this route extend beyond express conditions while remaining distinguishable from assurances creating procedural expectations? The manuscript provides criteria, but the literature audit cannot establish their completeness.
limitations: The complete supplied manuscript, including its bibliography, was read. External works were inspected at the locations recorded below; availability of a full text does not mean the entire work was read.

All eight bibliography entries were located and their identities checked. No material misquotation or misattribution was demonstrated in the inspected passages. This is not certification of every claim made by those sources.

Eule's publisher abstract, metadata, and exposed notes were accessible, but the article body was not. The attempted full-text URL was https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1747-4469.1987.tb00542.x. Its argument cannot be reconstructed from the abstract or notes alone.
Collingridge's book was located through a bibliographic preview, but substantive book pages were not retrieved. Secondary descriptions and search snippets were not used to establish its argument.

NEA's 2011 report at https://www.oecd-nea.org/rwm/rr/documents/RR-Final-Report_GD.pdf and the 2012 brochure download at https://www.oecd-nea.org/jcms/upload/docs/application/pdf/2020-11/7085-reversibility.pdf could not be fetched. The accessible 2001 report supplied the substantive NEA comparison.

The separate Van de Poel Table 3 URL failed. The article's accessible prose discusses the numbered conditions and their moral status, supporting the manuscript's relevant attributions without relying on an unseen table.

Dorf and Sabel's direct PDF opening initially failed, but opening the independently located search result subsequently returned the author-hosted text. Wallsten's current public article opened successfully; the manuscript's statement about an earlier failed opening is not thereby disproved. Its unspecified archived capture was not available for version comparison.

The care counties, feasible preparations, and three-month transition are expressly hypothetical assumptions. They were not treated as empirical findings requiring external confirmation. The manuscript contains no equations or attributed formal theorems to verify.

The search covered multiple formulations and neighboring literatures but was finite. It cannot establish exhaustive originality, absence of an earlier derivation, or absence of relevant work outside the retrieved material.
